claims.nodeLabel: Element 115: the Lazar claim and moscovium
claims.sourceText: Physical Review C 69, 021601(R), 2 February 2004; and Emile Kinley-Gauthier, 'The Strange Case of Bob Lazar', Skeptic, 23 April 2026, https://www.skeptic.com/article/the-strange-case-of-bob-lazar/ , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: THE COLLISION, STATED WITHOUT OVERSTATEMENT AND WITHOUT SOFTENING. Nothing about moscovium is stable, machinable, storable or available in gram quantities: it is produced one atom at a time at cross sections of about one picobarn and its decay chains run to completion within seconds. That is a direct contradiction of the claim's central requirement. It is NOT a refutation of the existence of element 115, which was never in dispute and was predicted long before 1989. Skeptic magazine's April 2026 treatment states the position correctly: IUPAC recognition 'does not validate Lazar's specific claims about a stable isotope or gravity propulsion'.
